documents.summary: University-wide guidance centered on data classification, an approved platform (Copilot), no AI detectors, and sample syllabus statements in three tiers. It also covers research use. Course-level AI decisions are left to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule for coursework: 'Instructors have discretion over whether and how generative AI tools fit their course's learning outcomes' and it offers three sample syllabus tiers, so it delegates. Its firm rules concern data and tools, not course stance.

units.why: The opening statement frames the university's position as welcoming 'responsible exploration' of generative AI, an institution-level principle; P56 (framework preamble) fits better than P02 because it sets a general stance without a per-use rule.
units.anchor: Lamar University supports responsible exploration of generative AI tools.
units.frag_end: academic integrity when using these tools.

units.why: Names the concerns users must keep in mind ('information security, data privacy, compliance standards, copyright, and academic integrity'), a general caution addressed to all users; coded as framework principles.

units.why: Defines generative AI ('a form of artificial intelligence trained on large datasets to produce content such as text, images, music, video, and code'), which sets scope; P61 definition.

units.why: Warns that the 'most likely response' is not necessarily accurate and 'Generated content must be critically evaluated before use'; verification duty on all users, P31.
